Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

used to verb

of the past: I used to play

also would (of habit), didn’t use to, once (in the past)

classical

Aug. Conf. 1.9.15: quia lūdēbam pilā puer
Cic. Sen. 44: saepe vidēbam puer

lūdēbam, vidēbam

the imperfect tense

I used to play, I used to see

The imperfect alone says what went on, or was done again and again, in the past; saepe, ōlim or puer (as a boy) make the habit plain.

Other words

  • soleō, solēre, solitus sum — be in the habit of; in the imperfect, used to

    verb, second conjugation, semi-deponent, with an infinitive · also used · classical · Ov. Ars 2.341: quem taurum metuis, vitulum mulcēre solēbās; Mart. 13.14.1: clūdere quae cēnās lactūca solēbat avōrum

    Names the habit outright; for the present, see usually. “Be used to” (accustomed) is another verb: adsuēscō (assuēscō), as Milo vitulum adsuēverat ferre, had got used to carrying the calf (Quint. 1.9.5).

Examples

  • quia lūdēbam pilā puer

    because as a boy I used to play ballAug. Conf. 1.9.15

  • C. Duellium … redeuntem ā cēnā senem saepe vidēbam puer

    as a boy I often used to see old Gaius Duilius coming home from dinnerCic. Sen. 44

  • quem taurum metuis, vitulum mulcēre solēbās

    the bull you are afraid of, you used to stroke when it was a calfOv. Ars 2.341

  • clūdere quae cēnās lactūca solēbat avōrum, dīc mihi, cūr nostrās inchoat illa dapēs?

    Lettuce used to close our grandfathers’ dinners: tell me, why does it open ours?Mart. 13.14.1–2

  • ut Milō, quem vitulum adsuēverat ferre, taurum ferēbat

    as Milo carried as a bull the animal he had got used to carrying as a calfQuint. 1.9.5

See also usually, would, be.
